The user wants docker compose up to start all services without requiring additional commands.

The backend healthcheck uses curl, but the eclipse-temurin:21-jre image lacks it. This causes the healthcheck to fail and prevents the frontend from starting properly.

The frontend Dockerfile copies the Next.js standalone build correctly. A .dockerignore file should be added to prevent copying host node_modules into the image.

The backend JRE image is Debian-based, so curl is not installed. Adding curl via apt-get or switching to wget would fix the healthcheck. Using a Java command directly is another option. The frontend can start before the backend is fully ready because its home page does not depend on the API.

The README should lead with `docker compose up --build` as the primary local path, keeping Gradle and npm as optional alternatives. A backend `.dockerignore` should exclude `.gradle` and build directories to speed up image builds. The final plan must include running `docker compose up --build` and verifying service health.

Gradle wrapper and network access during the Docker build could cause bootJar failures. The Spring Boot 3 actuator endpoint is confirmed at `/actuator/health`. Installing curl via apt-get inside the Dockerfile is the most reliable fix, since wget may also be absent in the JRE image.

The frontend should wait for the backend to report healthy before starting. The documented one-command path is `docker compose up --build`, while subsequent runs can use plain `up` or `-d`.
